title: Simulated power, page 10
published: The MTurk versions of the experiments studied here typically employ 500 subjects per treatment arm, suggesting that we would be well powered (power $\approx$ [[0.8]]) to detect treatment effect heterogeneity on the scale of 0.2 SD, and moderately powered for 0.1 SD (power $\approx$ [[0.6]]).
corrected: The MTurk versions of the experiments studied here typically employ 500 subjects per treatment arm, suggesting that we would be [[moderately]] well powered (power $\approx$ [[0.6]]) to detect treatment effect heterogeneity on the scale of 0.2 SD, and [[poorly]] powered for 0.1 SD (power $\approx$ [[0.1]]).
note: The simulation results the article deposits, and which Figure 4 is drawn from, give a rejection probability of 0.61 at 0.2 SD and 0.15 at 0.1 SD, both at 500 subjects per treatment arm. Figure 4 draws guide lines at 500 subjects and at power 0.8 and annotates the 0.2 SD curve where it crosses the second of them, which the simulation puts at 600 subjects per arm rather than 500; the sentence reads the height of the guide line rather than the curve. At those rejection probabilities the test is moderately well powered at 0.2 SD rather than well powered, and poorly powered at 0.1 SD rather than moderately so, and both descriptions are corrected with the numbers. The figure itself is correct and is not reprinted here.

title: Significant heterogeneity tests on the TESS/GfK sample, page 10
published: On the TESS/GfK replications, [[0]] of 10 tests were significant.
corrected: On the TESS/GfK replications, [[1]] of 10 tests were significant.
note: The deposited output file for Table 2 records 1 significant TESS/GfK test, and so does the maintained pipeline; the count does not move with the change R 3.6.0 made to `sample()`, which moves the other two rows of that column. Table 2 prints 2 in the TESS/GfK row of its N Significant column and 1 in the Original row, which is that column read in the row order of the deposited output file rather than in the table's own; the two entries are interchanged. Correcting the table requires the pre-R-3.6.0 sampler, so it is documented in the repository rather than reprinted here.

title: The description of statistical power, page 11
published: Because we are [[relatively]] well powered to detect politically meaningful differences in treatment response, I conclude from this evidence that the treatment effect homogeneity explanation of the correspondence across experimental sites is plausible.
corrected: Because we are [[moderately]] well powered to detect politically meaningful differences in treatment response, I conclude from this evidence that the treatment effect homogeneity explanation of the correspondence across experimental sites is plausible.
note: The sentence rests on the power figures of entry 1. At the corrected rejection probabilities, 0.61 at 0.2 SD and 0.15 at 0.1 SD, the tests are moderately well powered rather than relatively well powered, which is the description entry 1 now gives them. The conclusion the sentence draws is unchanged.
